result:
The audit of `/account-recovery/` is complete. The validator passed all 58 of 58 checks (0 missing, unknown, duplicate, blocked or not-run). The page is a static account page with no JavaScript and two forms: create an account, and reset a password.

**Scorecard**

```
Overall: 85/100 (needs work)

Speed & Stability      95  good
Memory Health         100  good
Usability & UX         73  needs work
Inclusivity & Reach    83  needs work
Discoverability & AI   85  needs work
Trust & Resilience     75  needs work

Do these first:
  1. [critical] Add a real sign-in form first on the page (email autocomplete="username webauthn" + current-password); make sign-up and recovery secondary
  2. [high] Back /signup and /reset with POST handlers: redirect to "verify your email" / neutral "if an account exists we emailed a link" pages; on failure re-render with input kept and an error summary
  3. [high] Serve over HTTPS with an enforced CSP, nosniff, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and a Secure HttpOnly session cookie
```

The interactive report is at `reports-cpa/127_0_0_1_8765/scorecard.html`. Its History tab now holds two runs, but they audit different pages on the same host (the earlier `/booking/` audit and this one). Read the deltas there as two pages compared, not one page improving.

**Main findings**
- **No way to sign in.** The heading says "Sign in or create an account", but there is no sign-in form or link, and `/signin` and `/login` return 404. Returning users can only create a new account.
- **Both forms dead-end.** Submitting either form returns a raw "501 Unsupported method" error page. This server is a static test fixture, so production may behave differently.
- **Passwords over plain HTTP, with no security headers**, while the footer tells users their account "is protected by a session cookie".
- **The reset field is labelled with a question.** Screen readers announce the email box as "Forgot your password?", and that form has no heading.
- **Password-only sign-up.** There is no passkey option, no show-password toggle and no stated password rule.

Also reported: no dark mode; buttons lose their outline in forced-colours mode; the nav's "current page" marker points at a directory listing; a fixed 16px body font; and a generic title with no meta description.

The run is in `reports-cpa/127_0_0_1_8765/2026-10-09T00-17-28-543Z/` (`report.json`, `report.md`, `evidence/`). I updated `latest.txt` to point at it. Nothing was committed. I made no source changes because this was report-only mode.

**TLDR:** All 58 checks judged (18 issues, 30 pass, 10 not applicable), producing 15 findings: 1 critical, 2 high, 7 medium and 5 low. Evidence came from screenshots under dark, narrow and forced-colours conditions, the axe accessibility scanner, the accessibility tree with a real Tab walk, target sizes, a CSS census, layout, a throttled mobile trace, a network recording, security headers, cookies, trackers, a secrets scan, a crawler-view comparison, an offline reload, before/after memory snapshots, my own form and endpoint probes, and Modern Web Guidance. The single highest-leverage fix is adding a real sign-in form, because returning users currently cannot sign in at all.
